profile.summary: BPNet is a convolutional neural network that predicts transcription-factor binding from DNA sequence at single-base resolution. It reads a stretch of genomic sequence and predicts the strand-specific read profile and the total read count of a ChIP-nexus or ChIP-seq experiment over that region. It is not a pretrained model: users train a new BPNet on their own experiment, then interpret it to find the sequence motifs that drive binding.

summary_quotes.text: We introduce a deep learning model, BPNet, that uses DNA sequence to predict base-resolution ChIP-nexus binding profiles of pluripotency TFs.
BPNet is a python package with a CLI to train and interpret base-resolution deep neural networks trained on functional genomics data such as ChIP-nexus or ChIP-seq.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: In the paper, the body of the network is a first convolutional layer of 64 filters of width 25 bp, followed by 9 dilated convolutional layers of 64 filters of width 3, with the dilation rate doubling at every layer and no pooling, so base resolution is kept. Two output heads per transcription factor sit on top: a deconvolutional layer that predicts the probability of a read at each position on each strand (profile shape), and a global average pooling layer with a fully connected layer that predicts the total read count. The loss is a multinomial negative log-likelihood for profile shape plus a mean squared error on log total counts. A control track is given as an extra input so that experimental bias is regressed out. After training, contribution scores and TF-MoDISco are used to extract motifs.

quotes.text: The first convolutional layer uses 64 filters of width 25 bp, followed by 9 dilated convolutional layers (64 filters of width 3 in each layer) where the dilation rate (number of skipped positions in the convolutional filter) doubles at every layer.
To preserve base resolution, pooling is not used.

a deconvolutional layer (filter width=25, typical ChIP-nexus footprint width) predicting the strand-specific probabilities of observing a particular read at a particular position in the input sequence (shape or profile prediction)
a global average pooling layer followed by the fully connected layer predicting the total number of read counts aligned to the input sequence for each strand (total read count prediction)

BPNet uses a multi-scale loss function to separately evaluate the predictions of profile shape (using a multinomial negative log-likelihood loss) and total read counts (using a mean squared error loss).
The signal from this track is regressed out during training, which prevents BPNet from learning these experimental biases.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There are two generations of the code in the same repository. The original package that accompanied the paper is kept at the v0-final tag; it uses a `bpnet train` command, a dataspec.yml file and Python 3.6 with TensorFlow 1. The current master branch is described by its authors as the improved version and the one to use; it has separate `bpnet-train`, `bpnet-predict` and `bpnet-shap` commands, Python 3.7, and an example configuration with a 2114 bp input, a 1000 bp output profile, a first filter of width 21 and 8 dilated layers. The two generations use different defaults, so a result should name the code version (tag or commit), the architecture parameters file and the training data. The trained mouse ESC model from the paper (Oct4, Sox2, Nanog, Klf4) is published on Zenodo and on Kipoi as BPNet-OSKN.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Paper version: a convolutional layer of 64 filters of width 25 bp, then 9 dilated convolutional layers (64 filters of width 3) with residual skip connections, no pooling, and per-factor profile and total-count heads. Current README example: first filter width 21, 8 dilated layers of 64 filters, profile head kernel 75.

facts.value: DNA sequence from a reference genome (2114 bp in the current README example), plus optional control (bias) bigWig tracks. Training also needs signal bigWigs for each strand and a BED file of peaks.

facts.value: Predicted strand-specific base-resolution read profiles and total read counts (1000 bp output in the current README example), written as test metrics and optional bigWig tracks; contribution (SHAP) scores per base from bpnet-shap.

strengths.text: Predicts binding at single-base resolution, because the network uses no pooling and models the full read profile on each strand.

quotes.text: To preserve base resolution, pooling is not used.
BPNet uses multi-task learning to jointly train on the strand-specific ChIP-nexus profiles of all four TFs.

strengths.text: The package covers the whole path from training to interpretation: prediction tracks, per-base contribution scores, and motif discovery with TF-MoDISco and motif hit calling with FiNeMo.

quotes.text: In our case we will assign each nucleotide an importance value or how much it contributed for the binding at each input region according to our model.
This step allows one to get a list of sequence motifs that drive the signal in the studied experiment.

strengths.text: Code is MIT licensed, and the trained paper model is on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0.

limitations.text: There is no general pretrained model. Each use needs a new model trained on aligned reads from a specific experiment, plus peak calls, a reference genome and preprocessing with samtools, bedtools and bedGraphToBigWig.

run_guide.summary: Install the current BPNet package, train a model on one prepared ChIP-seq experiment and predict profiles on held-out chromosomes.
prerequisites: A machine with an NVIDIA GPU, drivers and CUDA is recommended for training.
Miniconda, used to create a Python 3.7 environment.

Prepared data for one experiment: plus and minus strand signal bigWigs, a filtered peaks BED file, optional control bigWigs and GC-matched background regions, hg38 reference FASTA, chromosome sizes and a chroms.txt list. The README points to wiki pages for these steps (Download-test-data, Preprocessing, Outlier_removal, Background_generation).
input_data.json, bpnet_params.json and splits.json written as in the README tutorial.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create --name bpnet python=3.7
conda activate bpnet
steps.explanation: Creates and activates a Python 3.7 conda environment.

steps.title: Install BPNet and helper tools
steps.shell:
pip install git+https://github.com/kundajelab/bpnet.git
conda install -y -c bioconda samtools=1.1 bedtools ucsc-bedgraphtobigwig
steps.explanation: Installs the package from the repository's default branch, which may be newer than the commit read here, and the tools used to build bigWig tracks.

quotes.text: conda install -y -c bioconda samtools=1.1 bedtools ucsc-bedgraphtobigwig

steps.title: Choose the counts loss weight
steps.explanation: Computes the counts loss weight to put in the loss_weights field of bpnet_params.json.

steps.title: Train
steps.shell:
BASE_DIR=ENCSR000EGM
DATA_DIR=$BASE_DIR/data
MODEL_DIR=$BASE_DIR/models
REFERENCE_DIR=reference
CHROM_SIZES=$REFERENCE_DIR/hg38.chrom.sizes
REFERENCE_GENOME=$REFERENCE_DIR/hg38.genome.fa
CV_SPLITS=$BASE_DIR/splits.json
INPUT_DATA=$BASE_DIR/input_data.json
MODEL_PARAMS=$BASE_DIR/bpnet_params.json

mkdir $MODEL_DIR
bpnet-train \
        --input-data $INPUT_DATA \
        --output-dir $MODEL_DIR \
        --reference-genome $REFERENCE_GENOME \
        --chroms $(paste -s -d ' ' $REFERENCE_DIR/chroms.txt) \
        --chrom-sizes $CHROM_SIZES \
        --splits $CV_SPLITS \
        --model-arch-name BPNet \
        --model-arch-params-json $MODEL_PARAMS \
        --sequence-generator-name BPNet \
        --model-output-filename model \
        --input-seq-len 2114 \
        --output-len 1000 \
        --shuffle \
        --threads 10 \
        --epochs 100 \
        --batch-size 64 \
        --reverse-complement-augmentation \
        --early-stopping-patience 10 \
        --reduce-lr-on-plateau-patience 5 \
        --learning-rate 0.001
steps.explanation: The README's training command for the ENCODE CTCF example ENCSR000EGM. The README notes training may take a few minutes to start.

steps.title: Predict on the test chromosomes
steps.shell:
PREDICTIONS_DIR=$BASE_DIR/predictions_and_metrics
mkdir $PREDICTIONS_DIR
bpnet-predict \
        --model $MODEL_DIR/model_split000 \
        --chrom-sizes $CHROM_SIZES \
        --chroms chr7 chr13 chr17 chr19 chr21 chrX \
        --test-indices-file None \
        --reference-genome $REFERENCE_GENOME \
        --output-dir $PREDICTIONS_DIR \
        --input-data $INPUT_DATA \
        --sequence-generator-name BPNet \
        --input-seq-len 2114 \
        --output-len 1000 \
        --output-window-size 1000 \
        --batch-size 64 \
        --reverse-complement-average \
        --threads 2 \
        --generate-predicted-profile-bigWigs
steps.explanation: Runs the trained model on the test chromosomes from splits.json, in the same shell as the training step so the variables are set. The README's sample splits.json also lists chr21 under train, so remove it from one list before treating the test set as held out.

outputs: Test-set metrics in the predictions_and_metrics directory, and predicted profile bigWig tracks because --generate-predicted-profile-bigWigs is given.
